name: Do older homes in North Hollywood and Glendale need asbestos testing before gutting?

mainEntity.name: If a home was built before modern standards, when is asbestos testing or other hazardous-material testing needed before demolition?
mainEntity.text: If a home was built before modern standards, when is asbestos testing or other hazardous-material testing needed before demolition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before gutting an older home, hazardous-material testing should be considered early, especially if the structure was built before modern building standards. Materials such as floor tile, adhesive, insulation, ceiling texture, pipe wrap, and joint compounds may contain asbestos or other hazards. Testing is important before demolition begins because once materials are disturbed, abatement rules and safety procedures can change the project sequence. Homeowners should ask the contractor what testing is required, who is responsible for arranging it, and how the findings affect cost and schedule. If hazards are found, the project may need specialized removal before general demolition can continue. This should be built into both the budget and timeline so there are no surprises after work has already started.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older homes often need hazardous-material testing before demolition because materials such as insulation, flooring, mastic, or drywall compounds can contain asbestos or other hazards. Testing is especially important before disturbing walls, ceilings, or flooring in pre-modern homes. Failing to test can delay the project and increase safety risks.
